newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China detains senior CADTIC officials - papers.
newsitem.headline: China detains senior CADTIC officials - papers.

text.p: Senior officials from the China AgriBusiness Development Trust and Investment Corp (CADTIC) have been detained in Beijing for investigations in connection with embezzlement, newspapers reported at the weekend.
A senior CADTIC delegation, including its general manager, was taken into custody last Tuesday after having been summoned to Beijing for a seminar, the Chinese-language Ming Pao said.
Its managers have also been accused of embezzling up to 100 million yuan (US$12.05 million), the Sunday edition of the South China Morning Post reported.
The newspapers did not say where the officials were based.
The reports could not be independently confirmed in Beijing.

CADTIC, one of China's largest investment trusts, was placed under administrative custody of two state banks last week for what Chinese bankers have explained was an overextension of its business due to serious mismanagement.
CADTIC's domestic business had been taken over by the China Construction Bank while its overseas business had become the responsibility of the Bank of China.
CADTIC is the second largest shareholder of Hong Kong-based Seapower International Holdings Ltd with a 19.35 percent stake and has three directors on the board.

Seapower Group said in a statement last week that it had been informed that CADTIC has ceased its business. But it added it not been informed of any proposed transfer of CADTIC's shares in Seapower International or any proposed change in directors of the group.
